REFERRAL LETTER
Date: 10/17/2026
Patient Name: Grace Reed
DOB: 03/01/1977
MRN: MRN-60473

To: Cardiology Clinic Intake
From: Dr. Thomas Carter, Harbor Family Practice

Dear Colleague,

Reason for referral: Evaluation of chest pressure with exertion.

Grace Reed is a 49-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. For several weeks, she has experienced intermittent chest pressure when walking briskly or climbing stairs. It improves with rest and has led her to limit exertion.

Please evaluate her exertional chest pressure and advise on further care.

Thank you for seeing this patient.

Dr. Thomas Carter
Harbor Family Practice

PROGRESS NOTE
Date: 09/29/2026
Patient Name: Grace Reed
DOB: 03/01/1977
MRN: MRN-60473
Provider: Dr. Thomas Carter

SUBJECTIVE:
Grace Reed is a 49-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes who reports intermittent chest pressure with brisk walking or climbing stairs for several weeks. The pressure improves with rest and has led her to limit exertion.

VITALS:
BP 140/79, HR 62, RR 12, SpO2 96% on room air, weight 153 lb.

EXAM:
General: alert, no acute distress.
Neck: no jugular venous distension.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: no peripheral edema.

DATA REVIEWED:

Patient is on warfarin.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Exertional chest pressure. Symptoms improve with rest and are limiting activity. Cardiology referral placed for further evaluation. Advised not to push through symptoms and to seek urgent care for persistent or worsening pressure, symptoms at rest, or associated shortness of breath or fainting.
2. Atrial fibrillation. Known history. Coordinate ongoing care with cardiology during evaluation of exertional symptoms.
3. Hypertension. Continue routine follow-up and management with established care team.
4. Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Continue routine follow-up and management with established care team.
